title: Safety profile comparison of chimeric live attenuated and Vero cell-derived inactivated Japanese encephalitis vaccines through an active surveillance system in Australia.
ehr_evidence: Data were retrieved from SmartVax ( www.smartvax.com.au ), an active surveillance system for monitoring vaccine safety utilized by more than 450 clinics and other immunization providers in major cities and regional areas, in all states and territories throughout Australia including general practices, travel medicine clinics, and other immunization clinics (public, council, and hospital).
summary: Post-marketing safety comparison of chimeric live attenuated (Imojev) and Vero cell-derived inactivated (JEspect) Japanese encephalitis vaccines using active surveillance data from Australian clinics.
key_findings: No significant difference in odds of overall (OR = 1.27; 95%CI: 0.91–1.77), systemic (OR = 1.23; 95%CI: 0.74–2.06), or local (OR = 1.20; 95%CI: 0.65–2.22) AEFIs between Imojev and JEspect.
Higher odds of overall (OR = 2.39; 95%CI: 1.10–5.19) and local (OR = 4.13; 95%CI: 1.08–15.74) AEFIs observed in patients aged <5 years compared to >50 years.
No statistically significant interaction between sex and number of concomitant vaccines, though a trend suggested increased AEFI odds in females with more vaccines.
captured_features: specific symptoms (tiredness, headache, pain, swelling, rash, fever, etc.)
study_design: observational cohort study using active vaccine safety surveillance
population: 2756 patients receiving Japanese encephalitis vaccines at Australian clinics (median age 34 years, 52.6% female)
limitations: small sample size for children <5 years and lack of symptom severity data
AEFI intensity difficult to ascertain in young children
limited to 5-day post-vaccination follow-up due to SMS timing
small subgroup sizes prevented statistical analysis for some vaccine combinations and sex
